claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
- The name(s) of your child/children
- Their age(s) or date(s) of birth

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're asking about **Alex, who is 13 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the category that requires me to check some additional criteria. Let me proceed with the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is an important eligibility check for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 13, so he's still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for confirming that Alex doesn't work and is still in school. That's a "yes" to the question, since he's working less than 24 hours per week (in fact, not working at all).

Let me move to the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** Specifically, is he not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

(It's fine if he receives benefits through a parent/guardian - this is asking about benefits in his own name.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 13-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's another positive answer. Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits in his own name. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's only 13 and in school, I'm guessing the answer is no - but I need to confirm. If he is in any kind of apprenticeship, please let me know what type and which country it's in, as different regions have different rules.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just in regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular school and not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next stage of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?** 

Or, if you don't normally live in the UK, do you have any of the following:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and meet certain conditions like working, actively seeking work, having sufficient resources, or studying)
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad in a qualifying country

Let me know your residency situation, and I'll determine if you meet the requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you're living abroad, let me ask a few more questions to determine if you meet any of the special residency pathways for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Do you have settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** (This applies if you're an EU/EEA or Swiss national)

2. **Are you a Crown servant?** (For example, working for the UK Government, Foreign Office, or in certain qualifying roles abroad)

3. **Which country are you currently living in?**

These details will help me determine if you qualify under any of the special circumstances for claiming Child Benefit from abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have settled or pre-settled status. I'm not a Crown servant either. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided:

- You don't normally live in the UK
- You don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're not a Crown servant
- You're living abroad with your family

Unfortunately, this means you don't meet any of the special residency pathways required for Child Benefit eligibility. Child Benefit is a UK benefit that requires the claimant to normally live in the UK or meet one of the specific exceptions I mentioned.

Let me confirm this by checking the system:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**What this means:** Child Benefit can only be claimed by people who normally live in the UK, or who meet specific exceptions (such as having settled EU status, being a Crown servant abroad, or living in certain qualifying countries). Since you don't fall into any of these categories, you're not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Next Steps:**
- If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK to normally live here, you could reapply for Child Benefit
- You may be eligible for other support depending on where you're living and your circumstances - it's worth checking what benefits or support are available in the country you're currently in
- If you believe your residency status has changed or if you have pre-settled status that you didn't mention, you may want to get specialist advice

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that makes sense. Thank you for checking for me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify your situation. 

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you move back to the UK to live permanently—feel free to come back and we can reassess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

In the meantime, I hope you and Alex are doing well abroad. If you have any other questions about benefits or need further assistance, don't hesitate to reach out.

Take care! 😊

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you, I appreciate your help. Take care!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're very welcome! Thank you for using the Child Benefit eligibility assessment. Take care, and best wishes to you and Alex! 👋
